text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian newspapers this morning.
-Electricity prices continue to fall. Several power producers now sell electricity at prices similar to those of six or seven years ago.
-All board members of Norwegian insurer Storebrand voted yes to the proposed merger with Norway's second largest bank Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse at a meeting on Tuesday.

-State-owned oil company Statoil has had no luck so far in its bidding for oil field blocks in Venezuela. About 130 companies from around the world are competing for blocks in Venezuela's 20 oil fields.

-Private investor Tharald Broevig says he will increase his stock of Storebrand shares and vote against the proposed merger with Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse. Broevig is concerned that the government's shareholding in the merged company will be too strong. The Norwegian state holds 51 percent of shares in Christiania Bank.
-Sales of new cars declined during the first five months of 1997, but motorcycle sales rose by 51 percent compared to the same year-ago period.
-Norwegian industrial holding group Aker RGI is appealing to the finance ministry a ruling that the shareholdings of four investors in insurer Storebrand would be seen as one entity.
-Companies controlled by Norwegian shipping company Tschudi & Eitzen have made a 700 million kroon bid for the privatisation of Estonian Shipping Company Eesti Merelaevandus.
